Improving quality can lead to reduced costs through several mechanisms. Firstly, improved responses to customer inquiries can lead to increased sales, as satisfied customers are more likely to return and recommend the company to others. This, in turn, can result in increased revenue, which can be used to offset the costs of improving quality.

Flexible pricing can also be a key driver of cost reduction. By offering competitive pricing, companies can attract more customers and increase sales, which can help to offset the costs of improving quality. Furthermore, a good reputation can also lead to increased sales, as customers are more likely to choose a company with a reputation for quality and reliability.

Reducing rework and scrap costs is another way in which improving quality can lead to cost savings. When products are of high quality, they are less likely to require rework or scrap, which can be a costly process. Additionally, improving quality can also lead to lower warranty costs, as defective products are less likely to require costly repairs or replacements.

Overall, improving quality can lead to reduced costs through a combination of increased sales, flexible pricing, and a good reputation. By reducing rework and scrap costs, and lower warranty costs, companies can also increase productivity and reduce waste. This can lead to significant cost savings, which can be reinvested in the business to drive further growth and improvement.
